verdict: Caution: lend selectively to cashew processors with clean working-capital discipline and verified raw-material cover; avoid thinly capitalised, single-mill units with stretched limits.
title: Mangaluru Cashew Processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Cashew processing is a raw-material conversion trade: you buy raw cashew nut, shell, peel, grade and pack, and sell kernels to buyers who set the price.** Value sits in the raw nut and in the working-capital cycle, not in the machine. The local picture is thin: the only Mangaluru-specific cashew item in our file is a government plan to invest ₹1 crore in grafted saplings through KCDC [3], and a local report that domestic production is low and processors import raw nuts to meet processing demand [3]. So lean on first principles and peers here, and say so in the file. ## Where cash and value sit
**The cash is trapped between nut purchase and kernel sale, and the industry itself is fragmented with low entry barriers and limited pricing power** [10]. Labour dependence and periodic labour shortage further squeeze bargaining position [11]. **So when a proposal lands, check the raw-nut cover and the buyer book first; if the unit cannot show graded sales contracts, ask for the last six months of buyer-wise invoices.**

## What has changed now
**The national demand signal is weak: India-wide exports are -9.8% Apr-to-date in USD** [D]. Karnataka's local economy is running ahead — GST collections +11.1% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1%, and electricity demand +23.3% versus India +9.5% [D] — but that is a state-level tailwind, not a cashew-specific one. Rating reports show working-capital stress building in the sector: average utilisation around 50% in FY2025 rising to around 73% in 9M FY2026 at one entity [8], and over 90% with limited buffer at another [11]. **So treat limit utilisation as the first screen; if utilisation is above 90%, ask for the drawing-power statement and the stock-and-book-debt position before any enhancement.**

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue integrated processors with own or contracted raw-nut supply, mechanised lines and a diversified buyer base** — the Aelea and Sampoorna profiles [4][7] show scale and margin are achievable. **Avoid single-mill, single-buyer units that live on ad-hoc imported nut parcels** [3][10]. The ₹1 crore sapling programme [3] is a supply-side positive only over years, not a reason to lend today. Collect from customer: local raw-nut arrival volumes, district-wise processing capacity, and current kernel export prices. ## How to grow safely
**Structure against the nut, not the building: stock-and-receivables limits, monthly stock statements, and a covenant that raw-nut purchases are backed by confirmed orders.** Take every month: stock statement, debtor ageing, limit utilisation, and labour-days worked. **If utilisation crosses 90% [11], freeze enhancements and ask for the buyer-wise realisation statement.**
